subject: hierarchical model works fine on simulated data but does not converge on real data

messages.author: 188806804221876c
messages.subject: hierarchical model works fine on simulated data but does not converge on real data
parts:
Hello, I have the following model (shown later).
It runs fine and shows good results if I fit data generated according to the same generative model (or slight modifications of it). I performed simulation with  50 groups.

On real data I can fit 5-10 groups, but I have problems of convergence when I arrive to 15-20 groups.
I have 100 observations for each group.

The warning message which I get is 
1: There were 4000 divergent transitions after warmup. Increasing adapt_delta may help. 
2: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems

Increasing adapt_delta did not solve the problem.
The pairs plot show (when the model is fit on real data) that the posterior of the parameters is multimodal.
The Rhat is around 2 for the various parameters and the n_eff between 3 and 200.

I suspect the problem might lie in the multivariate likelihood statement.
Notice that my covariance matrix is patterned: all the elements on the diagonal are sigma2, all the entries outside diagonal are rho*sigma2.
rho is equal for all groups.
I exploit this structure to implement a robust computation of the inverse of the covariance matrix. So the issue should not be related to the covariance matrix. 

 data {
    real std_within; //empirical std within groups
    real std_among; //empirical std between groups

    int<lower=2> Nsamples; //number of results for each group.
    int<lower=1> q; //number of groups. 

    matrix[q,Nsamples] x; //observations (Nsamples for each group).
    

    real rho; //correlation between the observations of the same groups

     }



  transformed data {
    //here I build some quantities which do not depend on the data. Pretty sure the problem does not lie here as they are identical for simulated and real data.. 

    //parameters of the prior for sampling the sigma of each data set
    real unifLo;
    real unifHi;
    
    //matrixes which do not depend on the data and which are helpful to compute the likelihood
    vector[Nsamples] H;
    vector[Nsamples] zero_mean_vec;
    matrix[Nsamples,Nsamples] invM;
    real detM;
      
    /*determinant of M, whose expression is analytically known and does not depend on the data */
    detM <- (1+(Nsamples-1)*rho)*(1-rho)^(Nsamples-1);

    unifLo <- std_within/1000;
    unifHi <- std_within*1000;
    
    
    for (j in 1:Nsamples){
        zero_mean_vec[j]<-0;
        H[j]<-1;
       for (i in 1:Nsamples){
                if (j==i)
      invM[j,i]<- (1 + (Nsamples-2)*rho)*pow((1-rho),Nsamples-2);
        else
      invM[j,i]<- -rho * pow((1-rho),Nsamples-2);
       }
    }
    //at this point invM contains the adjugate of M.
    //we  divide it by det(M) to obtain the inverse of M.
    invM <-invM/detM;
  }

  parameters {
    real mu0; //mean of the  hyperprior
    vector[q] mu;               // mean of each group
    vector<lower=0>[q] sigma;   // variance  each group
  }

  model {
    real partial_lik; //lik of the j-th group
    real det_Sigma;
    
  
    //sample the data given the pars
    for (j in 1:q) {
        mu[j] ~ normal (mu0, std_among); 
        sigma[j] ~ uniform( unifLo, unifHi);
        det_Sigma <- pow(sigma[j],2*Nsamples) * detM;
            
        //computation of the multivariate likelihood based on the pre-computed inv(M)
        partial_lik <- -0.5 * 1/pow(sigma[j],2) * ( (x[j])' - H*mu[j] )' * invM * ((x[j])' - H*mu[j]);
        partial_lik <- partial_lik - 0.5 * log (det_Sigma) - 0.5*Nsamples*log(6.283);


        increment_log_prob(partial_lik);   
       }
  }

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] hierarchical model works fine on simulated data but does not converge on real data
parts:
May I ask you what you read before trying this? This
is like the third message with the same problem in the
last couple of days.

As a hint, you need to declare all your parameters so
that any values satisfying the constraints has support
in the model. Your sigma violates that principle.

Each divergent iteration should also print a warning message.
If that's not done by default, one of the R developers
should be able to help.

- Bob
